observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of two human hands cradling a smooth orange balloon. The foreground (right) hand's index and middle fingers, with visible fingernails, rest pressed against the balloon's lower-left surface, while a second, more blurred hand supports it from behind/left. The background is an out-of-focus gray indoor surface with a faint horizontal edge. The balloon's top is cropped by the frame edge throughout.
visible_changes: The balloon occupies progressively more of the frame: its left silhouette edge moves steadily leftward (roughly x~530 at t=0 to x~425 at t=1.6s), and it increasingly occludes the supporting hand and background on the left.

The foreground fingers remain in contact with the balloon but drift downward and leftward in image coordinates (index fingertip from ~y310 to ~y730), i.e. away from the balloon's center, while their apparent size stays roughly constant.
The specular highlight on the balloon's upper-left surface shifts down and left across the frames.
The blurred horizontal background edge drifts slightly downward over the segment, indicating a small camera/hand repositioning rather than a fixed viewpoint.
The balloon's top edge stays cut off by the frame at both ends; no inflation onset or completion is seen inside the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the balloon is actively being inflated (air added) or simply repositioned relative to the camera/hand; the cause of the size change is not visible.
What happened before t=0 and after t=1.6s (the action is already underway at the start and may continue past the end).
The identity/intent of the person holding the balloon.
uncertain_details: Object motion vs camera motion: the constant apparent size of the fingers argues against a pure zoom, but a small camera tilt/pan cannot be separated from hand movement given the blurred background.
Whether the leftward growth of the balloon's edge is true expansion (inflation) or the balloon translating toward the camera while the hand holds it.
Exact roles of the two hands (which is squeezing vs supporting) are not determinable from the frames.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
